title: Relative tensor-pullback homology comparison
statement: Let f:X -> S be a morphism of schemes, with the fixed derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback], and derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Let E be in D(O_X), K a complex of O_X-modules, and eK:Q(K) ≅ E. Put R=f-inverse O_S and restrict K along the tensor-pullback ring map [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let P be an R-module complex, K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], with a quasi-isomorphism q:P -> K restricted to R. For every O_S-module F, with inverse image [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module], and every integer i, the underlying abelian sheaf of H^i(E tensor^L Lf*(F[0])) is isomorphic to the underlying abelian sheaf of H^i(Tot(P tensor_R f-inverse F[0])) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. No finite Tor amplitude, boundedness, quasi-coherence, coherence or geometric assumption is imposed.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma 20.27.4, Tag 08DE; Tag 08EV, second displayed equality

proof.text: Resolve F[0] by a bounded-above flat complex L, zero above zero. Termwise tensor pullback computes its derived pullback. Exact inverse image carries L to a K-flat resolution of the inverse-image module.

Choose an O_X K-flat resolution A of K. The K-flat derived tensor comparison computes E tensor Lf*(F[0]) by A tensor f*L. In each bidegree the balanced tensor identity A tensor over O_X (O_X tensor over f-inverse O_S f-inverse L) = A restricted to f-inverse O_S tensor f-inverse L commutes with the signed differentials. Direct-sum totalization gives the restricted complex comparison.

Since inverse-image L is K-flat, tensoring it with the quasi-isomorphism zigzag A restricted -> K restricted <- P gives quasi-isomorphisms: apply the tensor-cone identity and the defining acyclicity criterion for K-flatness. Since P is K-flat, its tensor with inverse-image L -> inverse-image F[0] is also a quasi-isomorphism. Exact restriction of scalars commutes with homology, as does the exact functor to abelian sheaves. Apply homology in degree i to the zigzag, the localization homology comparison, and eK. This yields the asserted abelian-sheaf isomorphism, independently of any Tor interval or bound.
